outlets.title: Casper Testing Traffic Lights That Turn Green When Drivers Honk CASPER - A new traffic-control system being tested in Casper allows drivers to request a green light by honking their horn. Microphones installed at several intersections detect approaching vehicles and change the signal when enough drivers indicate they are ready to proceed. Engineers originally programmed the system to require three short honks. Within hours, drivers discovered that holding the horn continuously also works. Traffic officials say the technology has successfully reduced average wait times at participating intersections. Noise complaints have increased approximately 4,800%. One nearby resident said the intersection outside his home now sounds like “a wedding in India being attacked by geese.” Engineers are considering adjusting the system to recognize polite honking only. Nobody has determined what that sounds like.
